content: macro has a noWs keyword to say "Don't allow any whitespace between these two parts of the syntax". notation does not have anything like that. In #45029, I add a similar noWs keyword for notation3, which is @Kyle Miller's port of Lean 3's notation.

Kyle's plan for notation3 was to eventually integrate its functionality into notation in a principled way. Unfortunately, Kyle is busy. Therefore there is tension between extending notation3 and keeping the upstreaming of notation3 to core credible.
My question therefore is: Will the FRO want to add a noWs keyword to notation in the future and, if so, are you happy with the syntax I suggest in #45029 ?

Note that the noWs syntax for notation/notation3 cannot be the exact same as for macro since the syntax of the latter quotes all parts of the syntax being defined, while the syntax of the other two leaves them unquoted.
My shot-from-the-hip opinion is that I would prefer a macro attribute that tries to infer a delaborator
Hm. Maybe it is not as bad with correct highlighting in the editor
Yes indeed my noWs in notation3 is highlighted in blue, so it stands out compared to the rest of the notation definition
